page.layout: One page of running text. Running head at the top: the book title "HABAKUK" with its chapter reference "Cap. II: 5-8", and the page number 394 at the left. Below it a centred heading, "HISTORIA IMPLEMENTI.", in capitals. Then one column of text, with a section mark "§. I." at the left of the first paragraph and a woodcut initial. Italic verse in an indented block, then a citation line, and the catchword "Ita" at the bottom right. No marginal notes.

main_text.l: HISTORIA
IMPLEMENTI.
§. I. Voniam filum sermonis hujus Prophe-
tici nos ad ea deduxit tempora,
quæ adventum Christi consequerentur:
nulla hic alia Monarchia intelligi potest,
quam Romana, sub quâ Christus
natus spem patrum adimplevit, euangelium regni Christi
incepit, respublica Judæorum excisa, & ecclesia Christi inter
multas persecutiones conservata fuit. Non diffite-mur
varia esse prædicata, quæ monarchiæ Babylonicæ
possent accommodari; quia in genere cujuscunque mo-
narchi characteres exprimunt. Verum agnoscendum quoque
ea omnia longe potiori jure in Romanum qua-
drare imperium, quam in quodcunque aliud. Roma-
num imperium (si primarium expendamus charac-terem, qui
est amplitudo regni) præ omnibus latissimè regni-vit.
De hac regni amplitudine sic cecinit Virgilius Æ-neid.
libr. vi. quasi præsagiens.

l.i: Augustus Cæsar, Divum genus, aurea condet
Secula, qui rursus Latio, regnata per arva
Proferet imperium. Jacet extra sidera tellus,
Extra anni solisque vias, ubi cælifer Atlas
Axem humero torquet stellis ardentibus aptum. &c.

main_text.l: Idem. libr. vii. Nepotes

l.i: Omnia sub pedibus, quâ sol utrumque recurrens

page.notes: The text is clear throughout. The woodcut initial "V" is read as "Voniam" in the printed form "Uoniam", with the consonant U written as V. "Nepotes" on the citation line is printed as it stands, although it reads oddly there. The section mark "§. I." is kept as printed. The catchword "Ita" is at the bottom right.
